title: hub-erp configuration document (hub-erp/config/1)
description: Everything in force on a hub, as `hubproto config export` and GET /api/config write it, and as `hubproto config propose` and a change order's upload read it (hubproto.configjson). Written with sorted keys and a stable order of every list, so one configuration is always the same bytes. On propose, a part or policy section left out is left as it is; one that is given says the whole of it. See docs/design/config-json.md.

schema.description: The format and its version. A later, incompatible format gets another number.

release.description: The policy release the document was taken from. Propose refuses a document taken from another release than the one in force (it would undo what was released since).

version.description: Its version number: 1 is the first release to take effect. Read only.

effective_from.description: When it took effect (ISO 8601). Read only.

versions.description: The versions in force of what a change order may change without a new policy release. When given, propose refuses a document whose versions are not those in force.

forms.description: Record type -> the version of its released layout (types still on the hub's base layout are not listed).

policy.description: The rules of the policy release, one section per kind of rule. Each entry is the rule as the hub keeps it (hubproto.rules.KINDS), without its kind and its source: the section says the kind, and the source is the SOP sentence, which the change order's review round writes for a changed rule. A rule stated in several SOPs is one entry. Entries are sorted by their canonical JSON.

committees.description: kind committee: {name, group, chair, purpose, members?, quorum?}

permissions.description: kind permission: {subject: role:x|group:x|cog:x, action, object, resource: folder:<path>, effect: allow|deny|propose, confirmer?}

routing.description: kind routing: {process, step, condition: object|null, assignee, mode: assign|notify}

approval_criteria.description: kind approval_criteria: {approver: cog:x, process, max_amount, currency, conditions: [condition], countersign?, adversarial_reviews?, also_currencies?, max_per_day?, max_amount_per_month?}

segregation_of_duties.description: kind sod: {object, roles: [a, b], only?, rule?}

processes.description: kind process: a whole workflow (numbered steps, or statuses and transitions), as the workflow editor carries it

cogs.description: kind cog (a cog profile): {name, model, about?, persona?, prompt_from?, references?}

personas.description: kind persona: {name, stance, behaviour, tone?, lenses?, passes?, escalates?}

responsibilities.description: kind responsibility, READ ONLY: each SOP's Roles and responsibilities rows {frame, who, text}. Propose refuses a change: revise the SOP on a change order.

scopes.description: kind scope, READ ONLY: the scoping documents {name, level, compiles, layers_on}. Propose refuses a change.

record_types.description: Record type -> its definition, as config/record-types.json writes one (prefix, digits, yearly, object, fields, required_by_state, defaults, retention, sensitivity, gapless, system_fields, decision_fields, ...). Without the custom x_ fields of form layouts (they belong to the forms part). On propose only non-destructive changes are carried (hubproto.recordtypes); a type or field left out, a renamed or retyped field and a removed enum option are refused.

forms.description: Record type -> its form layout in force (hubproto.formlayout): {type, sections: [{id, title, fields: [{field, label?, help?, placeholder?, widget?, visible_when?, required_when?, readonly_when?}]}], start: [{field, widget?, spec?, input?}], custom_fields: {x_name: {type, label?, retired?}}, hidden?}. A layout that differs from the one in force is carried as the forms editor carries a draft; a type left out keeps its layout.

links.description: The link vocabulary: relation -> the label its inverse shows on the other record (lowercase names: letters, digits, hyphens). A relation left out is removed, which is refused while a link uses it or the hub's own steps link with it.

retention.description: The retention classes: class -> how long a record is kept and what its Track must hold. A class left out is removed, which is refused for standard, a class a record type is kept under, or one records are labelled with.

items.description: A rule without kind and source; a `kind` given must be the section's.
